subject: Geofence scope & operational failover windows — confirmation and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@cloudhealth.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geofence scope and failover windows - initial questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick onboarding session last week — we ran it by our security team and have a couple of clarifying asks before we move to signatures. High level we need to confirm:

1) For EU customers: can you confirm all inference processing (tokenization, KV cache, model execution) will be pinned to EU region resources under the hosted plan? We need to be sure no transient hops to US or APAC occur except under an explicit failover scenario.

2) Failover window: our policy allows transient cross-border processing for incident-driven failover, but we require a defined maximum window (our initial baseline is 48 hours) and an operational notification SLA (who to notify, evidence logs). Is Redwood able to commit to a max transient failover window and provide audit evidence when it happens?

3) KMS/keys: what options do you support for regional KMS? Can we bring our own key (BYOK) for EU? If not, what encryption-at-rest boundaries exist?

4) Subprocessors: please share the most recent roster and indicate which subprocessor endpoints may be involved in transient routing (CDN, analytics, telemetry).

We attached our DPA checklist and the subprocessor template — please respond with a short note we can send to Legal to track acceptance, and any DPA addendum you think is required.

Appreciate a reply with suggested language we can include in the DPA. If easier, we can hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Miller
Head of Security Programs
CloudHealth Inc.

--- Attachment: CloudHealth_Redwood_DPA_ask.pdf (summary checklist)
--- Attachment: requested_subprocessor_list_2027-05.csv (fields: name, role, region, endpoint)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Miller <sara.miller@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence scope and failover windows - initial questions

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Legal), Karthik (Ops), and Laura (Product) to make sure we cover both contractual and operational pieces. Below is a concise response and a proposed DPA addendum outline we can share with you.

Short answers up front:
- Region pinning: Yes — Redwood Hosted can be configured with EU-region pinning for inference. That configuration ensures inference compute, KV caching, and transient storage used by the runtime remain in the EU region by default.
- Transient failover: We support a defined transient failover policy. Our standard transient window historically used in large customers has been 72 hours, but we can discuss tightening to 48 hours with appropriate operational constraints. Any cross-region processing is done only when capacity or regional outage dictates.
- Notification & evidence: We provide an operational incident notification within 24 hours of an automated cross-region failover and include time-stamped routing logs (CSV) + request traces for the window. We can add a contractual clause to that effect.
- KMS/BYOK: For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys in select regions — EU BYOK is available via our KMS partner integrations (customer must provision key in their cloud account). For Dedicated/Private deployments BYOK is standard.
- Subprocessors: Attached is our up-to-date roster. We flag components that may be involved during transient routing.

Proposed DPA addendum (high level) — please review, this is what we would include in the contract and DPA:
- Definition: "Transient cross-border processing" = temporary routing of inference requests outside of the pinned region to maintain availability during outages, limited to a maximum cumulative window per incident.
- Max window: 72 hours standard; optional 48-hour negotiated cap for accounts with stricter locality requirements.
- Notification SLA: Redwood to notify primary CloudHealth security contact within 24 hours of an event and provide routing logs within 48 hours.
- Evidence: Time‑stamped routing traces, list of endpoints involved (IPs/domains), and a post-incident summary.
- KMS: BYOK support where available; if not available, encryption keys managed by Redwood KMS with region-bound key material and access logs.
- Escrow/mitigation: Option to require temporary rate limiting or failback policy executed by Redwood on request.

Next steps: Marissa — can your team propose language that maps the bullet points above into DPA clauses (coverage of notifications, windows, and evidence)? Karthik — please confirm operational feasibility of 48-hour vs 72-hour SLAs and what telemetry/logs we can commit to within 48 hours vs 72 hours. Laura — we should document BYOK availability in EU for this account.

Sara — happy to get on a 30 min call tomorrow. Proposed times: Tue 10:00-11:30am UTC or Tue 15:00-16:00 UTC. Which works for you?

Best,
Vivek
SVP, Sales & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--- Attachments sent: Redwood_DPA_v3_addendum-draft.pdf (working draft)
--- Attachments sent: requested_subprocessor_list_2027-05.csv (Redwood annotated)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, sara.miller@cloudhealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence scope and failover windows - initial questions

Thanks Vivek — quick legal note to start. We can map the proposed language into DPA text. A couple of suggested changes / asks from Legal:

- Max window: recommend we default to 72 hours in the DPA but include a customer-selectable checkbox for 48 hours during negotiation. That gives Ops breathing room during major outages.
- Notification & evidence: we can commit to notifying within 24 hours and delivering routing logs + trace samples within 48 hours; full packet-level traces may not be available for privacy reasons, but request/response traces and routing headers are available.
- SLA carveouts: we should add carveouts for third-party subprocessor outages and force majeure.

Operational ask for Karthik: please confirm whether we can produce a CSV of routing logs (timestamp, original region, routed-to region, request-id, node-id) and whether logs will include hashes only (no PII) — CloudHealth will need assurance that payloads are not output in logs.

Sara — Laura/Marissa are happy to work with your legal team to draft the final addendum. Vivek — I recommend a short joint call with CloudHealth legal + Security and Redwood Legal + Ops to sign off.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

--- Note: Redwood_DPA_v3_addendum-draft.pdf contains proposed clauses and change highlights for Legal review.

From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@cloudhealth.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudhealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence scope and failover windows - initial questions

Vivek / Marissa / team — thanks for the quick and thorough response. CloudHealth Legal and Security reviewed and we can accept the 72-hour default provided we get the following:

- A confirmable notification within 24 hours with routing logs (CSV) — these must include timestamp, request-id, original region, routed region, and the node-id. Hashes only for any user identifiers — no PII in logs.
- A binding clause that transient routing cannot be used for feature experiments or analytics — it must be incident-driven only.

On the KMS front: BYOK in EU is a hard requirement; if BYOK is not available in the hosted plan we will need to move to Dedicated. Please confirm the BYOK enablement checklist for EU (who provisions the key, which cloud partners are supported).

We are okay with starting the DPA negotiation with the 72-hour clause and an option to reduce to 48 hours for a higher-tier SLA. Please send an updated DPA addendum with the notification language and the routing log schema. After that we will route internally for final sign-off and procurement will follow with DocuSign.

I can do the call tomorrow (Wed) at 09:00-09:30 UTC. Let me know which calendar invite to accept.

Regards,
Sara Miller
Head of Security Programs
CloudHealth Inc.

--- Attachment acknowledged: CloudHealth_Redwood_DPA_ask.pdf
--- Request: Please provide the draft DPA addendum (redlines) + BYOK checklist before the call.
